q.s: The Neolithic site of Mehrgarh, which gives the earliest evidence of farming in the subcontinent, is located in:
q.x: Mehrgarh lies in the Kachhi plain of Baluchistan near the Bolan Pass; its Period I goes back to about 7000 BCE.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a pre-Harappan or Early Harappan site?
q.x: Lothal, the dockyard town in Gujarat, is a Mature Harappan site.

q.s: The Harappan city of Dholavira, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located on Khadir island in:
q.x: Dholavira lies on Khadir island in the Rann of Kachchh, Gujarat.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in Gujarat?
q.x: Kalibangan is in Rajasthan, on the Ghaggar.

q.s: The DNA study of a 4,600-year-old female skeleton, read as a challenge to the Aryan-invasion view, was done at the Harappan site of:
q.x: The Rakhigarhi skeleton lacked the 'Steppe Pastoralist' gene, which was read as indigenous ancestry.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in Haryana?
q.x: Lothal is in Gujarat; Rakhigarhi, Banawali and Bhirrana are in Haryana.

q.s: The Harappan site of Kalibangan in Rajasthan is located on the banks of the river:
q.x: Kalibangan is on the Ghaggar; Ropar is on the Sutlej and Rangpur on the Sukhbhadar.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Harappan site and river is NOT correct?
q.x: Harappa is on the Ravi.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT found at Mohenjodaro?
q.x: The red sandstone male torso was found at Harappa; the other three come from Mohenjodaro.

q.s: The famous ten-sign Harappan inscription signboard was found at:
q.x: The signboard belongs to Dholavira; Harappa is known for Cemetery H and two rows of six granaries.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with Harappa?
q.x: Harappa is associated with Cemetery H, the granaries and the red sandstone torso; the signboard is from Dholavira.

q.s: The Harappans' belief in an afterlife is inferred chiefly from:
o: Large quantities of gold buried with the dead
Pots, ornaments and mirrors buried with the dead
q.x: Pots, ornaments and copper mirrors were buried with the dead; on the whole the Harappans did not bury precious things.

q.s: Ahichchhatra was the capital of which Later Vedic kingdom?
q.x: Ahichchhatra (Rohilkhand) was the Panchala capital; Hastinapur was associated with the Kurus.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Later Vedic kingdom and its association is NOT correct?
q.x: Kurukshetra belonged to the Kurus; Videha lay beyond the Sadanira and was ruled by King Janaka.

q.s: 'The Light of Asia', a poem on the life of the Buddha, was written by:
q.x: Edwin Arnold's 'The Light of Asia' (1879) is based on the Lalitavistara.

q.s: Which philosopher was called 'Prachhanna Buddha' (crypto-Buddhist) by his critics?
q.x: Shankaracharya was called Prachhanna Buddha; Nigantha Nataputta was Mahavira.

q.s: In Buddhism, the Noble Truth that the world is full of suffering is called:
q.x: Dukkha is the first truth; Samudaya is the cause, Nirodha the cessation and Magga the path.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Four Noble Truths of Buddhism?
q.x: The four truths are Dukkha, Samudaya, Nirodha and Magga; ahimsa is an ethical principle, not one of them.

q.s: Chandragupta Maurya was succeeded on the throne by his son:
q.x: Bindusara (297-273 BCE) succeeded Chandragupta; Ashoka was Chandragupta's grandson.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Mauryan ruler?
q.x: Dhana Nanda was the last Nanda king, overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE.

q.s: The Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra under Ashoka was presided over by:
q.x: Moggaliputta Tissa presided over the Third Council; Vasumitra presided over the Fourth.

q.s: Which Ashokan edict expresses his faith in the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha?
q.x: The Bhabru (Bairat) minor rock edict states Ashoka's faith in the Three Jewels.

q.s: According to Megasthenes, the city of Pataliputra was administered by a board of:
q.x: Pataliputra was run by a board of 30 members in six committees of five each.

q.s: In Megasthenes' account, the officers in charge of roads, irrigation and land measurement were the:
q.x: The Agronomoi were district officers in charge of roads, irrigation and land measurement; the Astynomoi were city officers.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Mauryan pillars is correct?
o: They were built in pieces with a fluted shaft.
They are monolithic, baseless and smooth-shafted.
They always stand on a carved base like Persian pillars.
They were made of white marble from Makrana.
q.x: Mauryan pillars are monolithic, baseless and polished, unlike the segmented, fluted Achaemenid pillars; hence they are seen as an Indian adaptation.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Mauryan pillars?
q.x: Fluted shafts belong to Achaemenid pillars.

q.s: The founding of the Nalanda university (c. 450 CE) is credited to the Gupta ruler:
q.x: Kumaragupta I is credited with founding Nalanda; late in his reign the Pushyamitras and Hunas threatened the empire.

q.s: In Gupta administration, the Sandhivigrahika was the minister in charge of:
q.x: Sandhivigrahika was the minister of peace and war; the Akshapataladhikrita kept royal records.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Gupta official and function is NOT correct?
q.x: The Dutaka was a spy or messenger, not a revenue collector.

q.s: The gold coins issued in the largest numbers by the Guptas were called:
q.x: Gupta gold coins were dinaras; silver coins (rupakas) were issued after Chandragupta II defeated the Shakas.

q.s: Gupta silver coins were first issued after the defeat of the:
q.x: Chandragupta II issued silver coins after defeating the Shakas of western India.

q.s: The Harshacharita, a semi-historical biography of Harshavardhana, was written by:
q.x: Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita and the Kadambari, the latter completed by his son Bhushanabhatta.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Banabhatta?
q.x: Mudrarakshasa was written by Vishakhadatta.

q.s: In the Chola period, the term 'Irai' referred to:
q.x: Irai was the land tax; Vetti and Kudimai were forced labour; Ayam denoted royal dues.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a form of forced labour in the Chola period?
q.x: Irai was the land tax; Vetti, Muttaiyal and Kudimai were labour services.

q.s: The Fawaid-ul-Fuad, the record of the conversations of Nizamuddin Auliya, was compiled by:
q.x: Amir Hasan Sijzi recorded Nizamuddin Auliya's conversations in the Fawaid-ul-Fuad.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Nizamuddin Auliya is correct?
o: He belonged to the Suhrawardi order.
His conversations were recorded by Ziauddin Barani.
He never visited the royal court though he lived through several reigns.
q.x: He was a Chishti saint buried in Delhi; Amir Hasan Sijzi recorded his talks.

q.s: Rohtas Fort near Jhelum, built by Sher Shah Suri, was constructed under the supervision of:
q.x: Rohtas Fort was begun in 1541 under Todar Mal; it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

q.s: The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is located at:
q.x: Sher Shah's tomb is at Sasaram in Bihar.

q.s: During Aurangzeb's Rajput war of 1679-81, the claim of Ajit Singh of Marwar was championed by:
q.x: Durgadas Rathore championed Jaswant Singh's posthumous son Ajit Singh.

q.s: Which Mughal prince revolted against Aurangzeb, joined the Rajputs in 1681 and later fled to Sambhaji?
q.x: Prince Akbar, Aurangzeb's son, joined the Rajputs and later took refuge with Sambhaji.

q.s: The 'marble cancer' affecting the Taj Mahal is caused mainly by:
q.x: Sulphur dioxide pollution causes 'marble cancer'; the Supreme Court set up the Taj Trapezium Zone in the M.C. Mehta case (1996).

q.s: The Taj Trapezium Zone was demarcated by the Supreme Court in the case of:
o: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
Vellore Citizens' Forum v. Union of India
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
q.x: In the M.C. Mehta case (1996) the Court demarcated the Taj Trapezium Zone to shift or clean up industries.

q.s: Baz Bahadur, the musician-poet famous for his romance with Rupmati, was the last Sultan of:
q.x: Baz Bahadur was the last independent Sultan of Malwa, conquered by Akbar.

q.s: Which of the following statements about music at the Mughal court is correct?
o: Abul Fazl lists 36 singers at Akbar's court.
Baz Bahadur was a court musician of Jahangir.
q.x: Aurangzeb ended court music but played the veena; Tansen was at Akbar's court.

q.s: Ustad Mansur, the Mughal painter of flora and fauna, was given the title:
q.x: Jahangir gave Ustad Mansur the title Nadir-ul-Asr; Abul Hasan was Nadir-uz-Zaman.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Mughal artist and title is NOT correct?
q.x: The calligrapher Muhammad Husain Kashmiri was Zarin Qalam; Nadir-ul-Asr was Ustad Mansur.

q.s: The Bhakti saint Mirabai was married to Bhoj Raj, the son of:
q.x: Mirabai, a Rathore princess of Merta, married Bhoj Raj, son of Rana Sanga of Mewar.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Bhakti saints is correct?
o: Mirabai was married to Rana Sanga of Mewar.
Haridas Thakur, born a Muslim, was a disciple of Chaitanya.
q.x: Haridas Thakur was Chaitanya's disciple; Mirabai married Bhoj Raj, son of Rana Sanga, and Chaitanya, called Nimai, popularised sankirtan.

q.s: Shivaji was crowned and assumed the title 'Chhatrapati' at Raigarh in the year:
q.x: At the 1674 coronation at Raigarh, performed by Gaga Bhatta, Shivaji took the title Chhatrapati.

q.s: Shivaji's coronation at Raigarh in 1674 was performed by:
q.x: Gaga Bhatta (Vishweshwar) of Varanasi performed the coronation.

q.s: The first European power to establish a factory at Machilipatnam (1605) was the:
q.x: The Dutch set up the first European factory in Andhra at Machilipatnam in 1605; the English followed in 1611.

q.s: The English East India Company established its factory at Machilipatnam in:
q.x: The English factory at Machilipatnam dates from 1611; the French came in 1669.

q.s: Tantia Tope, the last major leader of the Revolt of 1857 to be executed, was hanged at:
q.x: Tantia Tope was hanged at Shivpuri in 1859.

q.s: Kunwar Singh, a leader of the Revolt of 1857, belonged to:
q.x: Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur (Bihar) died there on 26 April 1858.

q.s: Lord Canning described the loyal Indian princes during the Revolt of 1857 as:
q.x: Canning called the loyal princes 'breakwaters to the storm'; the revolt was chiefly of the Bengal Army.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Revolt of 1857 is correct?
o: It began in the Madras Army at Vellore.
The Gorkhas fought against the British.
The Madras and Bombay armies largely stayed loyal to the British.
Lord Dalhousie was Governor-General during the revolt.
q.x: The revolt was chiefly of the Bengal Army; Canning was Governor-General and the Gorkhas helped Colin Campbell.

q.s: Mir Qasim, Nawab of Bengal, shifted his capital and set up a gun factory at:
q.x: Mir Qasim set up his gun factory at Monghyr; he was placed on the throne in 1760 by Vansittart.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Mir Qasim is correct?
o: He was placed on the throne in 1760 by Vansittart.
His army was reorganised by the Frenchman Raymond.
He was the son of Mir Jafar.
He fought on the British side at Buxar.
q.x: Mir Qasim, Mir Jafar's son-in-law, had his army reorganised by Gurgin Khan and fought the British at Buxar.

q.s: Under the Dual Government in Bengal (1765-72), the naib diwan for Bengal was:
q.x: Reza Khan was naib diwan for Bengal and Raja Shitab Rai for Bihar.

q.s: The great Bengal famine of 1770 occurred when the Governor of Bengal was:
q.x: The 1770 famine came during John Cartier's governorship under the Dual Government.

q.s: The system of Dual Government in Bengal (1765-72) is associated with:
q.x: Clive introduced the Dual Government after obtaining the Diwani in 1765; it was abolished by Warren Hastings in 1772.

q.s: Which Viceroy's Calcutta Corporation Act of 1899 reduced the number of elected members, leading 28 members to resign?
q.x: Curzon's 1899 Act cut the elected members and increased the nominated ones.

q.s: The Bombay Municipal Act of 1872, which gave ratepayers the right to elect half the Corporation, was backed by citizens led by:
q.x: The 1872 Act was drafted and backed by citizens led by Pherozeshah Mehta.

q.s: Sharada Sadan, a home for widows, was founded by:
q.x: Pandita Ramabai founded the Sharada Sadan for widows in 1889.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of organisation and its work is NOT correct?
o: Arya Samaj – True knowledge of the Vedas
Prarthana Samaj – Revival of Vedic sacrifices
Satyashodhak Samaj – Justice for the lower castes
q.x: The Prarthana Samaj worked for women and the depressed classes; it did not revive Vedic sacrifices.

q.s: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used by the:
q.x: The Simon Commission first used the term; the Government of India Act, 1935 fixed it and the first list came in 1936.

q.s: Ambedkar's 'Annihilation of Caste' (1936) was prepared as an address for the:
q.x: When the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal withdrew its invitation, Ambedkar self-published the address.

q.s: Which of the following books was NOT written by B.R. Ambedkar?
q.x: Hind Swaraj (1909) was written by Gandhi.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a demand of the Moderates in the Indian National Congress?
o: Separation of the judiciary from the executive
q.x: Purna Swaraj was adopted only in 1929; the Moderates sought council reforms, separation of the judiciary and reduced salt tax.

q.s: The Age of Consent Bill (1891), backed by the Moderates, was opposed by:
q.x: The Moderates supported the Bill; Tilak opposed it.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Moderate leader of the Congress?
q.x: Tilak was an Extremist leader.

q.s: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) was founded at Nagpur in 1925 by:
q.x: K.B. Hedgewar founded the RSS at Nagpur on 27 September 1925.

q.s: The Hindu Mahasabha was founded in 1915 at Haridwar by:
q.x: Malaviya founded it in 1915, first as the Sarvadeshik Hindu Sabha; Savarkar became president in 1937 at Ahmedabad.

q.s: The 'crawling order' imposed in Amritsar after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre was issued by:
q.x: Dyer ordered Indians to crawl down the lane where Marcella Sherwood had been assaulted.

q.s: The committee appointed to inquire into the Jallianwala Bagh massacre was headed by:
q.x: The Hunter Committee (1919) inquired into the Punjab disturbances.

q.s: The Poona Pact between Gandhi and Ambedkar was signed on:
q.x: The Communal Award came on 16 August 1932; the Poona Pact followed on 24 September 1932.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the events of 1931-32 is correct?
o: The Communal Award was announced before the Poona Pact.
The Poona Pact preceded the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
The Second Round Table Conference was held in 1930.
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed after the Communal Award.
q.x: Gandhi-Irwin Pact March 1931; Second RTC Sept–Dec 1931; Communal Award 16 Aug 1932; Poona Pact 24 Sept 1932.

q.s: The August Offer of 1940 was made by the Viceroy:
q.x: Linlithgow made the August Offer on 8 August 1940, naming dominion status as the goal.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the August Offer of 1940?
o: Dominion status as the goal for India
No constitution without the consent of the minorities
Expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council
Complete independence as the immediate goal
q.x: The August Offer named dominion status, not complete independence, as the goal.

q.s: The Rani Jhansi Regiment of the Indian National Army was led by:
q.x: Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal led the all-women Rani Jhansi Regiment.

q.s: In the 2002 presidential election, Lakshmi Sahgal was defeated by:
q.x: Lakshmi Sahgal lost the 2002 presidential election to A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.

q.s: The first INA flag on the Indian mainland was hoisted in April 1944 at:
q.x: The INA flag was hoisted at Moirang, Manipur, on 14 April 1944.

q.s: The first Governor-General of Pakistan was:
q.x: Jinnah became the first Governor-General of Pakistan in August 1947.

q.s: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress at the time of Independence in August 1947?
q.x: Acharya J.B. Kripalani was Congress President in 1947.

q.s: The international airport at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district is named after:
q.x: Bhogapuram airport is named Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT named after Alluri Sitarama Raju?
o: An Agency district of Andhra Pradesh
q.x: The ASR district and Bhogapuram airport bear his name and the Bhimavaram statue is of him; Vijayawada's airport at Gannavaram is not named after him.

q.s: Gandhi took the word 'Harijan' from the writings of the Gujarati saint:
q.x: Gandhi adopted 'Harijan' from Narsinh Mehta.

q.s: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded by Gandhi in 1932 first under the name:
q.x: It began in 1932 as the All India Anti-Untouchability League.

q.s: At which session of the Andhra Mahasabha did Nyapati Subbarao propose a single administration for all Telugu areas?
q.x: Nyapati Subbarao's proposal came at the second Andhra Mahasabha (1914).

q.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement (1956) between the leaders of Andhra and Telangana was signed at:
q.x: It was signed at Hyderabad House, New Delhi, by eight leaders, four each from Andhra and Telangana.

q.s: How many leaders signed the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956?
o: Eight, five from Andhra and three from Telangana
Six, three each from Andhra and Telangana
Ten, five each from Andhra and Telangana
Eight, four each from Andhra and Telangana
q.x: Four leaders each from Andhra and Telangana signed it.

q.s: The committee set up in 2010 to examine the demand for a separate Telangana was chaired by:
q.x: The Srikrishna Committee had V.K. Duggal as Member-Secretary.

q.s: 'Sakala Janula Samme' in Telangana (2011) refers to a:
q.x: Sakala Janula Samme was a general strike of about 42 days in September–October 2011.

q.s: AMS dating that places the earliest iron in India at about 2172 BCE comes from the Tamil Nadu site of:
q.x: Mayiladumparai in Krishnagiri district gave iron dates of 2172 BCE.

q.s: Which of the following early iron-age / megalithic sites is NOT in Tamil Nadu?
q.x: Panayal, a rock-cut burial chamber, is in Kasaragod, Kerala.

q.s: The Western Kshatrapa ruler Rudradaman I belonged to the:
q.x: Chashtana and Rudradaman I were Kardamakas with their seat at Ujjain; Nahapana was a Kshaharata.

q.s: Nahapana, the Western Kshatrapa ruler of the Nasik-Junnar region, belonged to the:
q.x: Bhumaka and Nahapana were Kshaharatas.

q.s: The Ikshvakus, successors of the Satavahanas in Andhra, had their capital at:
q.x: The Ikshvakus ruled from Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda).

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Samanta rajya and its seat is NOT correct?
q.x: The Mahabhojas were in the Konkan.

q.s: In the early Amaravati sculptures, the Buddha is represented mainly through:
q.x: Early Amaravati panels show the Buddha through symbols; the human image spread under the Kushanas.

q.s: Which of the following schools of sculpture did NOT flourish in the early centuries CE?
q.x: The Pala school of eastern India flourished from the 8th century.

q.s: The Vishnukundin ruler Madhava Varma II married a daughter of the Vakataka king:
q.x: Madhava Varma II married a daughter of Prithvisena II.

q.s: Madhava Varma II took the title 'Trikuta-Malayadhipati' after defeating the:
q.x: His victory over the Anandagotrikas (Trikuta = Kotappakonda) gave him the title.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Vishnukundins is correct?
o: Their ship-marked coins point to the importance of sea trade.
They were feudatories of the Rashtrakutas.
q.x: Ship-marked coins and Madhava Varma II's title Trisamudradhipati indicate maritime activity.

q.s: The Kannada work 'Kavirajamarga' is associated with the Rashtrakuta ruler:
q.x: Kavirajamarga is attributed to Amoghavarsha I (or his court poet Srivijaya).

q.s: Arab writers referred to the Rashtrakuta kings by the name:
q.x: The Arabs called them 'Balhara', from Vallabharaja.

q.s: The Nandampudi grant of Rajaraja Narendra was composed by:
q.x: Nannaya composed the Nandampudi grant; its donee was Narayana Bhattu.

q.s: The Eastern Chalukya ruler who granted the village of Mushikonda to the Jains was:
q.x: Vishnuvardhana III made the Mushikonda grant to the Jains.

q.s: Which of the following Eastern Chalukya Jain grants is NOT correctly matched with its royal patron?
q.x: The Kaluchumbarru grant was made by Ammaraja II.

q.s: The Kumararama temple at Samalkot, one of the Pancharamas, was built by the Eastern Chalukya ruler:
q.x: Chalukya Bhima I built Kumararama (Bhimesvara) at Samalkot in memory of his son.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Pancharama temples of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Pancharamas are Amararama, Draksharama, Somarama, Ksheerarama and Kumararama; Amararama is the one on the Krishna.

q.s: The Chalukya-Vikrama era, which replaced the Saka era in royal records, was started in 1076 by:
q.x: Vikramaditya VI began the Chalukya-Vikrama era in 1076; his court poet Bilhana wrote the Vikramankadevacharita.

q.s: The Kalyani Chalukya ruler who granted Hanamkonda to the Kakatiya Prola I was:
q.x: Someshvara I Ahavamalla granted Hanamkonda to Prola I.

q.s: The Nellore Chodas of Andhra ruled from:
q.x: Vikrama Simhapuri is Nellore; the Konidena Chodas ruled from Kotyadona.

q.s: The first grammar of the Telugu language written in Telugu, 'Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam', was composed by:
q.x: Ketana wrote Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam; Nannaya's Andhra Sabda Chintamani was in Sanskrit.

q.s: Mula Ghatika Ketana dedicated his Dasakumara Charitra to:
q.x: Ketana dedicated Dasakumara Charitra to Tikkana, who gave him the title Abhinava Dandi.

q.s: The first Kakatiya ruler to come to Hanamkonda was:
q.x: Beta I was the first Kakatiya at Hanamkonda; he attacked Kanchi in 1051 for Someshwara I.

q.s: The Kakatiya ruler Prola II was killed in battle by the:
q.x: Prola II was killed by the Velanati Chodas.

q.s: The Kakatiya ruler Rudradeva was killed by the Yadava ruler:
q.x: Jaitugi killed Rudradeva; Mahadeva invaded the Yadava kingdom to avenge him.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Kakatiya ruler?
q.x: Singhana was a Yadava ruler of Devagiri.

q.s: The Kakatiya ruler Rudradeva (Prataparudra I) bore the title:
q.x: Rudradeva was called Vidyabhushana; Prola I was Arigajakesari.

q.s: In the Qutb Shahi administration of Golconda, the Mir Jumla was the:
q.x: The Mir Jumla was the finance minister; the Kotwal was the city police chief.

q.s: Which of the following Qutb Shahi terms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
q.x: The Mustasib (Mahasib) was in charge of public morals.

q.s: Harihara I of Vijayanagara took the title 'Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati' as recorded in an inscription of 1340 at:
q.x: The Badami inscription of 1340 records the title.

q.s: Which of the following dynasties did NOT rule the Vijayanagara empire?
q.x: Vijayanagara was ruled by the Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties; the Bahmanis were its rivals.

q.s: After the defeat at Talikota in 1565, Sadasiva Raya and Tirumala fled to:
q.x: They fled to Penukonda, which became the new Aravidu capital.

q.s: The historian H.K. Sherwani calls the Battle of Talikota (1565) the battle of:
q.x: Sherwani calls it the battle of Bannihatti; it is also called Rakshasa-Tangadi.

q.s: Which of the following castes did NOT arise from the Veerashaiva movement in the Kakatiya period?
q.x: Satanis and Dasaris came from Vaishnavism; Lingayats, Jangamas and Balijas from Veerashaivism.

q.s: Moturpha, a tax in the Madras Presidency abolished in 1861, was a tax on:
q.x: Moturpha was levied on looms, shops and artisans.

q.s: The Madras High Court replaced the Company's courts in the Madras Presidency in:
q.x: The Madras High Court was established in 1862 under the Indian High Courts Act, 1861.

q.s: The Indian Penal Code was enacted in:
q.x: The IPC was enacted in 1860; the Criminal Procedure Code followed in 1861.

q.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 abolished:
q.x: The Act abolished both zamindari and inamdari estates, with compensation to zamindars.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 is correct?
o: Zamindars were paid compensation under it.
It came into force on 26 January 1950.
It converted ryotwari lands into zamindari.
q.x: It abolished zamindari and inamdari estates with compensation and came into force on 7 September 1949.

q.s: The Telugu social drama 'Varavikrayam' was written against the evil of:
q.x: Varavikrayam by Kallakuri Narasimham attacks the dowry system.

q.s: 'Hindu Sundari' (1902), a Telugu journal, was devoted to the cause of:
q.x: Hindu Sundari espoused the women's cause; Zamin Ryot backed peasants.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of movement and the paper that backed it is NOT correct?
q.x: Hindu Sundari espoused the women's cause; Zamin Ryot backed the peasants.

q.s: Who is called 'Andhra Charitra Pitamaha'?
q.x: Komarraju Lakshmana Rao is called Andhra Charitra Pitamaha.

q.s: The Rajaraja Narendra Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was founded in 1904 at:
q.x: It was founded at Hanamkonda in 1904.

q.s: The first boat library ('padava yatra') in Andhra was organised in West Godavari in 1918 by:
q.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao organised the 1918 padava yatra.

q.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao linked the library movement with the:
q.x: He linked the libraries to the Home Rule League; Sarvottama Bhavan was opened in his honour in 1949.

q.s: The first Indian to receive the Kaula Gold Medal for library service was:
q.x: Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya, father of the Andhra library movement, received the Kaula Gold Medal.

q.s: In Rayalaseema, the folk art form Burrakatha is also known as:
q.x: Burrakatha is called Thandana Katha in Rayalaseema.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an instrument used in Burrakatha?
q.x: Burrakatha uses the Tambura, the Burra drum and the Gummata; the mridangam is not used.

q.s: The Kuchipudi dance form was founded by:
q.x: Siddhendra Yogi founded Kuchipudi; Kshetrayya was a composer of padams.

q.s: The village of Kuchipudi was gifted to its performers by the Golconda ruler:
q.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah gifted the village to the Kuchipudi Bhagavatulu.

q.s: The CPI (Maoist) was formed in 2004 by the merger of the People's War Group with the:
q.x: The PWG and MCC merged in 2004 to form the CPI (Maoist).

q.s: The Naxalbari uprising of 1967 took place in which district of West Bengal?
q.x: Naxalbari is in Darjeeling district.

q.s: In the Shilpa Sailesh case (2023), the Supreme Court held that it can dissolve a marriage on irretrievable breakdown under:
q.x: The Court used its power under Article 142(1); irretrievable breakdown is not a ground under the Hindu Marriage Act.

q.s: Which of the following statements about divorce on irretrievable breakdown of marriage is correct?
o: It is not a ground of divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
It was added to Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act in 2006.
The Supreme Court cannot grant it if one party opposes.
It is a statutory ground under the Special Marriage Act.
q.x: The Supreme Court grants it under Article 142; Naveen Kohli (2006) only urged that it be made a ground.

q.s: The book 'Homo Hierarchicus' on the Indian caste system was written by:
q.x: Dumont's Homo Hierarchicus (1966) explains caste through the opposition of pure and impure.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the creation of an autonomous State within Assam?
q.x: Article 244A was added by the 22nd Amendment, 1969.

q.s: Article 15(4), enabling special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes, SCs and STs, was added by the:
q.x: Clause 15(4) was inserted by the First Amendment, 1951.

q.s: The Delhi riots of February 2020 took place mainly in:
q.x: The 2020 riots were in North-East Delhi.

q.s: Which of the following statements about linguistic reorganisation of States is correct?
o: It was opposed by the Andhra Movement.
It removed all linguistic minorities from every State.
It was first carried out in 1971.
It created new linguistic minorities such as Telugus in Tamil Nadu.
q.x: Drawing State boundaries on language left some speakers as minorities in neighbouring States.

q.s: The Justice J.S. Verma Committee on amendments to criminal law (2013) included Leila Seth and:
q.x: The members were Justice Verma, Justice Leila Seth and Gopal Subramanium.

q.s: Which of the following did the Justice Verma Committee recommend?
o: Raising the age of consent to 18
q.x: It recommended criminalising marital rape and keeping the age of consent at 16; it did not favour the death penalty for rape.

q.s: At present, the legal minimum age of marriage for men in India is:
q.x: The marriage age is 18 for women and 21 for men.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the age of consent in India is correct?
o: The Law Commission's 283rd Report recommended lowering it under POCSO.
The legal age of marriage is 18 for both men and women.
The Madhya Pradesh High Court asked for it to be lowered to 14.
The Justice Verma Committee wanted the age of consent kept at 16.
q.x: The Law Commission advised against lowering it; the MP High Court asked for 16.

q.s: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme was launched on 22 January 2015 at:
q.x: BBBP was launched at Panipat; it addresses the declining child sex ratio.

q.s: The nodal Ministry for the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme is the Ministry of:
q.x: WCD is the nodal Ministry, with Health and Education; the scheme is fully centrally funded.

q.s: Under the National Social Assistance Programme, the National Family Benefit Scheme gives:
o: A lump sum on the death of the primary breadwinner
A pension to persons with severe disability
A pension to BPL persons aged 60 and above
q.x: NFBS gives a lump sum of Rs 20,000 on the death of the primary breadwinner of a BPL family.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the National Social Assistance Programme?
o: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme
q.x: AVYAY is a separate scheme for senior citizens; NFBS belongs to the NSAP.

q.s: Under the National Policy on Older Persons, 1999, an 'older person' is one aged:
q.x: NPOP 1999 defines older persons as those aged 60 or above.

q.s: The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE) is implemented by the Ministry of:
q.x: NPHCE (2010-11) is run by the Health Ministry, not MoSJE.

q.s: The SACRED portal of the Government of India is meant for:
q.x: SACRED (Senior Able Citizens for Re-Employment in Dignity) links job providers with senior citizens.

q.s: The Supreme Court judgment that recognised transgender persons as the 'third gender' (2014) is:
o: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
Shayara Bano v. Union of India
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
q.x: NALSA (15 April 2014) held gender identity to be a matter of self-identification.

q.s: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act was passed in:
q.x: Parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act in 2019, following the NALSA judgment.

q.s: NPS Vatsalya, launched in 2024, is a pension scheme meant for:
q.x: NPS Vatsalya lets parents open NPS accounts for their minor children.

q.s: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the assured pension after 25 years of service is:
o: 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months
50% of the last basic pay drawn
60% of the average basic pay of the last 10 months
40% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months
q.x: UPS gives 50% of the last 12 months' average basic pay after 25 years; the ₹10,000 minimum needs ten years.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the 'Talli Bidda Express' service is meant to:
o: Drop mothers and newborns home after delivery
q.x: Talli Bidda Express is the drop-back vehicle that takes the mother and newborn home.

q.s: The International Day of Persons with Disabilities, observed on 3 December, was proclaimed in 1992 by the:
q.x: The UN General Assembly proclaimed the Day in 1992.

q.s: Which body in Andhra Pradesh provides aids, appliances and economic rehabilitation to persons with disabilities?
o: AP Differently Abled and Senior Citizens Assistance Corporation
AP Social Welfare Residential Institutions Society
q.x: The AP Differently Abled and Senior Citizens Assistance Corporation provides aids and rehabilitation.

q.s: Which of the following ports is NOT located in Sri Lanka?
q.x: Chabahar is in Iran; India is upgrading Kankesanthurai port in Sri Lanka.

q.s: Hambantota port in Sri Lanka is often cited as part of the encirclement of India by:
q.x: Hambantota, leased to a Chinese firm, is seen as part of China's 'string of pearls'.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's position on arms control is correct?
o: India has signed the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons.
India has signed the NPT as a non-nuclear-weapon State.
India supports negotiating a non-discriminatory, verifiable FMCT.
q.x: India backs FMCT talks at the Conference on Disarmament but stays out of the NPT, CTBT and TPNW.

q.s: Which of the following has India NOT signed?
q.x: India stays out of the NPT, CTBT and TPNW.

q.s: The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) won the Nobel Peace Prize in:
q.x: The OPCW won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an organ of the OPCW?
q.x: A Board of Governors belongs to the IAEA; the OPCW has the Conference, Executive Council and Technical Secretariat.

q.s: The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) heads which department of the Ministry of Defence?
q.x: The CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs, created in 2019.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Chief of Defence Staff is correct?
o: The CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs.
The CDS exercises military command over the three Service Chiefs.
The post of CDS was created in 2016.
The CDS heads the Department of Defence.
q.x: The CDS post was created in December 2019; the CDS heads the DMA and chairs the Chiefs of Staff Committee without commanding the Service Chiefs.

q.s: The first Chief Justice of the Federal Court set up under the Government of India Act, 1935 was:
q.x: Sir Maurice Gwyer was the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court (1937).

q.s: Which of the following was abolished by the Government of India Act, 1935?
q.x: The 1935 Act abolished the Council of India and gave the Secretary of State advisers.

q.s: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of:
q.x: DPSP came from Ireland; 'procedure established by law' came from Japan.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of borrowed feature and source is NOT correct?
o: Residuary powers with the Centre – Canada
q.x: 'Procedure established by law' came from Japan.

q.s: Which of the following languages is NOT included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
q.x: Tulu is not scheduled; Bodo, Dogri, Santhali and Maithili were added by the 92nd Amendment, 2003.

q.s: Santhali was added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the:
q.x: The 92nd Amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Jain Tirthankara?
q.x: Ajita Kesakambalin was a materialist teacher; Parshvanatha was the 23rd and Mahavira the 24th Tirthankara.

q.s: The Adi Granth was compiled by:
q.x: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.

q.s: Adult suffrage for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies is provided in:
q.x: Article 326 provides adult suffrage; Article 324 deals with the Election Commission.

q.s: In Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006), the Supreme Court held the right to vote to be a:
q.x: The Court held voting to be a statutory right, provided under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

q.s: The protection of monuments and places of national importance is a Directive Principle under:
q.x: Article 49 directs the State to protect monuments; Article 51A(f) asks citizens to preserve composite culture.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A?
o: To value and preserve the heritage of our composite culture
To protect monuments of national importance
To protect and improve the natural environment
q.x: Protecting monuments is the State's duty under DPSP Article 49.

q.s: A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament is provided for under:
q.x: Article 108 provides for joint sittings, presided over by the Speaker.

q.s: Who presides over a joint sitting of Parliament in the absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker?
o: Senior-most member of the Lok Sabha
Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
q.x: The RS Chairman never presides; next after the Speaker and Deputy Speaker comes the Deputy Chairman.

q.s: The 13-judge bench in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) was headed by:
q.x: CJI S.M. Sikri headed the bench that laid down the basic structure doctrine.

q.s: The first judicial reference to the 'basic features' of the Constitution was made in Justice Mudholkar's dissent in:
q.x: Justice Mudholkar's dissent in Sajjan Singh (1965) first referred to basic features.

q.s: Which of the following is an extra-constitutional staff agency of the Prime Minister?
q.x: The PMO is not in the Constitution; the Cabinet is mentioned in Article 352.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the Constitution of India?
q.x: The post of Deputy PM has no constitutional basis; the Cabinet is mentioned in Article 352.

q.s: The first President of India to die in office was:
q.x: Zakir Husain died in 1969; Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed was the second, in 1977.

q.s: Which of the following Presidents of India did NOT serve as Vice-President earlier?
q.x: Sanjiva Reddy was never Vice-President; Giri, Narayanan and Zakir Husain were.

q.s: A short-duration discussion in the Lok Sabha is raised under:
q.x: Rule 193 discussions last at most two hours and carry no vote.

q.s: In the Lok Sabha, a privilege motion is raised under:
q.x: Rule 222 in the Lok Sabha; Rule 187 in the Rajya Sabha.

q.s: Which of the following States does NOT have a Legislative Council?
q.x: Six States have Councils: AP, Telangana, Bihar, UP, Maharashtra and Karnataka.

q.s: Which of the following statements about State Legislative Councils is correct?
o: Kerala and Rajasthan have Legislative Councils.
A Council can be created only by a constitutional amendment.
Parliament can create or abolish a Council on a resolution of the State Assembly.
q.x: Under Article 169 Parliament acts on an Assembly resolution, without a constitutional amendment; six States have Councils.

q.s: Under Article 170, the strength of a State Legislative Assembly shall be not more than 500 and not less than:
q.x: Exceptions include Goa and Mizoram (40 each) and Arunachal (minimum relaxed under Article 371H).

q.s: Which of the following statements about State Legislative Assemblies is correct?
o: Article 170 sets a maximum of 450 members.
No Assembly can have fewer than 60 members.
Goa and Mizoram have Assemblies of 40 members each.
Arunachal Pradesh's minimum is relaxed under Article 371A.
q.x: The range is 60-500; Arunachal's minimum is relaxed to 30 under Article 371H.

q.s: A no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers can be moved only in the:
q.x: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)).

q.s: The oath of secrecy to Union Ministers is administered by the:
q.x: The President administers the oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers.

q.s: The word 'Cabinet' appears in the Constitution only in Article:
q.x: It was inserted in Article 352 by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Council of Ministers and the Cabinet is correct?
o: The Council of Ministers meets regularly as a body.
The Cabinet is larger than the Council of Ministers.
The Cabinet directs and supervises the Council of Ministers.
q.x: The Cabinet is a smaller body within the Council, which rarely meets as a whole.

q.s: The Governor's report recommending President's Rule in a State is made under:
q.x: Article 356 deals with failure of constitutional machinery; Article 360 is the financial emergency.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Governor of a State?
o: Causing the CAG's State report to be laid before the Legislature
Reporting to the President under Article 356
Acting as Chancellor of Central universities in the State
q.x: The President is Visitor of Central universities; the Governor is Chancellor of State universities.

q.s: India's first mobile court was set up in August 2007 at Punhana in:
q.x: The first mobile court was at Punhana, Mewat district, Haryana.

q.s: The All India Judicial Service can be created under Article:
q.x: Article 312 enables the AIJS, which has not yet been constituted.

q.s: Instead of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the National Green Tribunal is guided by the principles of:
q.x: The NGT Act, 2010 frees the Tribunal from the CPC and binds it to natural justice.

q.s: The National Green Tribunal was set up under an Act passed in:
q.x: The National Green Tribunal Act was passed in 2010.

q.s: The special arrangements under Article 370 for Jammu and Kashmir were made inoperative in:
q.x: Article 370 provisions were made inoperative in August 2019 and the State was reorganised into two UTs.

q.s: The Goods and Services Tax came into force in India on:
q.x: GST came into force on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Amendment Act, 2016.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax is correct?
o: It was introduced by the 122nd Amendment Act.
It came into force on 1 April 2017.
q.x: GST is destination-based; the 101st Amendment Act was introduced as the 122nd Amendment Bill.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Law Commission of India is correct?
o: It is a constitutional body under Article 324.
It is an advisory body constituted by executive notification.
It submits its reports to the President.
q.x: It is set up for three years by executive notification and reports to the Ministry of Law and Justice.

q.s: The Universal Periodic Review of the human rights record of every UN member is conducted by the:
q.x: The UPR, begun in 2008, is run by the Human Rights Council.

q.s: The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) was set up in 1993 following the:
o: Vienna World Conference on Human Rights
q.x: The OHCHR was set up after the 1993 Vienna Conference.

q.s: The CBI needs the consent of the State Government to investigate in a State because 'Police' is a subject in the:
q.x: Police is Entry 2 of the State List; Section 6 of the DSPE Act requires State consent.

q.s: The Central Bureau of Investigation derives its legal powers from the:
q.x: The CBI functions under the DSPE Act, 1946.

q.s: Under Section 20 of the RTI Act, 2005, the maximum penalty that can be imposed on a Public Information Officer is:
q.x: The penalty is ₹250 per day up to ₹25,000; the burden of proof lies on the PIO.

q.s: Which of the following statements about penalties under the RTI Act, 2005 is correct?
o: The burden of proof lies on the Public Information Officer.
The Commission cannot recommend disciplinary action.
The burden of proof lies on the applicant.
q.x: The penalty is ₹250 a day up to ₹25,000, and the Commission may recommend disciplinary action.

q.s: Citizen Report Cards as a tool of public accountability were pioneered by the:
q.x: Samuel Paul's PAC, Bengaluru pioneered Citizen Report Cards in the 1990s.

q.s: 'Jan Sunwai' public hearings in Rajasthan in the 1990s were organised by the:
q.x: MKSS's Jan Sunwais helped spark the RTI movement.

q.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2005) was chaired by:
q.x: Veerappa Moily chaired the Second ARC, which submitted 15 reports between 2006 and 2009.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT recommended by the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: A Code of Ethics for ministers
Abolition of the All India Services
q.x: The 2nd ARC sought reform, not abolition, of the civil services.

q.s: The 6th Report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission dealt with:
q.x: The 6th Report was on Local Governance; the 5th on Public Order.

q.s: Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj on 2 October 1959 at:
q.x: Panchayati Raj was inaugurated at Nagaur; Andhra Pradesh followed later in 1959.

q.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee on Panchayati Raj (1977-78) recommended a:
q.x: It recommended Zilla Parishads and Mandal Panchayats, with the district as the pivot.

q.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee was appointed in 1977 by the Janata government headed by:
q.x: It was appointed in December 1977 under PM Morarji Desai and reported in August 1978.

q.s: The first State to launch Panchayati Raj Institutions in India was:
q.x: Rajasthan launched PRIs at Nagaur on 2 October 1959; Andhra Pradesh was second.

q.s: The first State to give 50% reservation to women in Panchayati Raj institutions was:
q.x: Bihar was the first to provide 50% reservation to women in PRIs.

q.s: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, PESA, was enacted in:
q.x: PESA (1996) extends Part IX to Fifth Schedule Areas and empowers Gram Sabhas.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the PESA Act, 1996 is correct?
o: It applies to the Sixth Schedule Areas.
It creates autonomous regions with legislative powers.
It was passed along with the 73rd Amendment in 1992.
It extends Part IX Panchayats to the Fifth Schedule Areas.
q.x: PESA empowers Gram Sabhas in Fifth Schedule Areas; it creates no legislatures.

q.s: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed every year on:
q.x: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993; National Voters' Day is 25 January.

q.s: The minimum age for contesting elections to Panchayats and Municipalities is:
q.x: The minimum age of 21 applies to both Panchayat and Municipal elections.

q.s: In tribal policy, the approach of development while retaining tribal identity, favoured by Nehru, is called:
q.x: Integration combines development with retention of identity; assimilation absorbs tribes into the mainstream.

q.s: Eklavya Model Residential Schools for tribal students are modelled on the:
q.x: EMRS are modelled on the Navodaya Vidyalayas; the scheme started in 1997-98.

q.s: Eklavya Model Residential Schools are run under the Ministry of:
q.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs runs EMRS; the target is 740 schools.

q.s: The headquarters of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) is at:
q.x: IRDAI, set up in 2000, is headquartered at Hyderabad.

q.s: The setting up of IRDAI was recommended by the:
q.x: The Malhotra Committee (1993-94) recommended an insurance regulator.

q.s: Grievances of pensioners at the Union level are handled on a separate platform called:
q.x: Pensioners use CPENGRAMS; general public grievances go to CPGRAMS.

q.s: The concept of the Citizens' Charter originated in 1991 in the United Kingdom under Prime Minister:
q.x: John Major launched the Citizens' Charter in 1991; India adopted it in 1997.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Citizens' Charters in India is correct?
o: They are enforceable in the High Courts.
They are issued by the Supreme Court.
q.x: Citizens' Charters, adopted in 1997 and coordinated by DARPG, are not legally enforceable.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's nuclear doctrine (2003) is correct?
o: It was adopted by the National Security Council.
Its Executive Council is chaired by the Defence Minister.
It permits first use against a large conventional attack.
It is based on No First Use and credible minimum deterrence.
q.x: The Cabinet Committee on Security adopted it; the Executive Council of the NCA is chaired by the NSA.

q.s: The Political Council of the Nuclear Command Authority, the only body that can authorise nuclear use, is chaired by the:
q.x: The Political Council is chaired by the PM; the Executive Council by the NSA.

q.s: Under the Supreme Court's 2018 Cauvery verdict, the largest share of water was allotted to:
q.x: Tamil Nadu got 404.25 TMC, Karnataka 284.75, Kerala 30 and Puducherry 7.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a party to the Cauvery water dispute?
q.x: The parties are Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala and Puducherry.

q.s: The National Population Policy, 2000 set the medium-term objective of bringing the Total Fertility Rate to replacement level by:
q.x: The NPP 2000 aimed at a TFR of 2.1 by 2010 and population stabilisation by 2045.

q.s: India's Total Fertility Rate fell to below the replacement level of 2.1 as per:
q.x: NFHS-5 recorded a TFR of 2.0.

q.s: The headquarters of UN-Habitat is located at:
q.x: UN-Habitat is at Nairobi; Habitat I was at Vancouver (1976) and Habitat III at Quito (2016).

q.s: The New Urban Agenda was adopted at Habitat III in 2016 at:
q.x: Habitat III at Quito adopted the New Urban Agenda.

q.s: The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana was launched in:
q.x: JRY came in 1989, after IRDP (1980) and before EAS (1993) and SGRY (2001).

q.s: Which of the following employment programmes was launched the earliest?
q.x: IRDP (1980) came before JRY (1989), EAS (1993) and SGRY (2001).

q.s: Which of the following pairs of scheme and Ministry is NOT correct?
o: National Career Service – Labour and Employment
q.x: Himayat, the J&K youth skilling scheme, is under the Ministry of Rural Development.

q.s: PM-SVANidhi provides collateral-free working capital loans to:
q.x: PM-SVANidhi is for street vendors, run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan is a pension scheme for:
q.x: PM-SYM covers unorganised workers aged 18-40 earning up to ₹15,000 a month.

q.s: Which of the following pension schemes is NOT meant for persons aged 18-40?
q.x: PMVVY (LIC) is for senior citizens aged 60 and above.

q.s: CAPART, set up in 1986 under the Ministry of Rural Development, mainly:
o: Funds voluntary organisations and promotes rural technology
q.x: CAPART funds voluntary agencies; Mission Antyodaya ranks Gram Panchayats.

q.s: After overtaking Japan in 2025, India's rank in the world by nominal GDP is:
q.x: India is 4th, behind the USA, China and Germany; it is 3rd by PPP.

q.s: By GDP at purchasing power parity (PPP), India ranks:
q.x: India is the third-largest economy by PPP, after China and the USA.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) is estimated by the:
q.x: The AP DES estimates GSDP in 9 sectors at 2011-12 prices.

q.s: As per PLFS 2023-24, how does Andhra Pradesh's overall labour force participation rate compare between rural and urban areas?
o: It is higher in urban areas
It is higher in rural areas
q.x: AP's overall LFPR is 50.1% in rural and 41.3% in urban areas.

q.s: India's Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted by the:
q.x: The PLFS is conducted by the NSO under MoSPI.

q.s: The dual-sector model of economic development, based on the movement of surplus labour from the subsistence to the modern sector, was given by:
q.x: Lewis's 1954 model explains development through transfer of surplus labour.

q.s: 'The Accumulation of Capital' (1956) was written by:
q.x: Joan Robinson wrote The Accumulation of Capital; Keynes is known for the paradox of thrift.

q.s: In the UNDP's Human Development Report, countries with an HDI value of 0.800 and above are classed as:
India, with an HDI value between 0.550 and 0.699, falls in which human development category?
q.x: India is in the medium human development category.

q.s: Which of the following statements about multidimensional poverty in India is correct?
o: The 24.82 crore estimate comes from the UNDP's Global MPI.
India's MPI headcount rose to 11.28% in 2022-23.
Andhra Pradesh's MPI value fell from 0.053 to 0.025.
Andhra Pradesh's MPI value rose from 0.025 to 0.053.
q.x: The 24.82 crore estimate is from NITI Aayog; the headcount fell to 11.28%.

q.s: The State moving to 'extreme-poverty-free' status in 2025 is:
q.x: Kerala declared itself free of extreme poverty.

q.s: The Satat Jeevikoparjan Yojana, a graduation-approach anti-poverty model, is run by:
q.x: Bihar runs it under its JEEViKA mission.

q.s: The State Bank of India was formed from the Imperial Bank of India in:
q.x: SBI was formed in 1955, during the First Five Year Plan.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a State tax?

q.s: Since which Amendment has the corporation tax become part of the divisible pool shared with the States?
q.x: The 80th Amendment (2000) brought all Union taxes into the divisible pool.

q.s: GST compensation to the States was paid for a period of:
q.x: Compensation ran for five years, from July 2017 to June 2022.

q.s: The 16th Finance Commission anchors the States' fiscal deficit at:
q.x: The 16th FC keeps the States' deficit anchor at 3% of GSDP.

q.s: Bitcoin, the first decentralised cryptocurrency, was created in 2009 by:
q.x: Bitcoin is private and decentralised; no central bank issues it.

q.s: The Self-Help Group-Bank Linkage pilot programme of 1992 was started by:

q.s: Which of the following statements about the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme is correct?

Only the State Bank of India lends to SHGs.

q.s: The convener of the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) in Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: Union Bank of India is the SLBC convener in AP.

q.s: The Service Area Approach in rural banking was introduced in:
q.x: Under the Service Area Approach (April 1989), each rural branch serves a set of villages.

q.s: The Basel II framework rests on three pillars: minimum capital requirements, supervisory review and:
q.x: Basel II (2004) has three pillars.

o: India began implementing Basel III in 1999.
Basel I set minimum capital at 12% of risk-weighted assets.
Basel I (1988) covered only credit risk.

q.s: Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs) in India are registered with the RBI under the:

100% FDI in SEZs always needs government approval.
SEZ proposals go directly to the Prime Minister's Office.
